metadata.title: 2010 Case 06
metadata.original_presentation: A 37-year-old man was seen in the oral and maxillofacial surgery clinic of this hospital because of a lesion on the tongue.

required.content: What symptoms did the patient initially present with?
required.response: Three weeks earlier, a painful lesion had developed on the tongue, associated with a tender nodule in the left neck.

teaching_points.content: Initial presentation of oral lesions can be indicative of various conditions, including infections and neoplasms.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical history?
required.response: History of borderline hypertension and asthma; tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy in the past.

teaching_points.content: Past medical history can provide context for current symptoms and potential complications.

required.content: What are the patient's social habits and lifestyle?
required.response: Sexually active with men, drinks alcohol socially, does not smoke or use illicit drugs, works in an office.

teaching_points.content: Social history, including sexual activity and substance use, can influence disease risk and management.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Tongue
key_features: risk factors include alcohol use and sexual activity

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Oral Candidiasis
refuting_evidence: tender nodule in the neck is unusual

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Traumatic Ulcer
refuting_evidence: tender nodule in the neck is unusual
additional_information_needed: detailed history of recent oral trauma or habits
oral examination for signs of irritation

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Oral Herpes Simplex Virus Infection
refuting_evidence: no history of recurrent oral herpes
additional_information_needed: viral culture or PCR from the lesion

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: Tender, irregular, shallow ulcerated lesion on the left ventral surface of the tongue; mobile, smooth, tender lymph node in the left anterior cervical chain; scattered areas of erythema and blisters on the lower legs.

teaching_points.content: Physical examination findings can help localize the disease process and guide further testing.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Tongue
key_features: painful ulcerated lesion on the tongue
supporting_evidence: tender nodule in the left neck

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Oral Syphilis
refuting_evidence: lesion is painful rather than painless

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Herpes Simplex Virus Infection
supporting_evidence: scattered blisters on the lower legs
refuting_evidence: no mention of vesicular lesions on the tongue
additional_information_needed: HSV PCR or culture from the lesion

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Oral Candidiasis
refuting_evidence: lesion is ulcerated rather than white patches

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Behçet's Disease
supporting_evidence: scattered blisters on the lower legs
refuting_evidence: no history of recurrent oral or genital ulcers

required.response: Culture of the tongue lesion was negative for HSV; culture of the cloudy blister on the foot grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus; punch biopsy of the tongue lesion; CT scans of the head and neck.

teaching_points.content: Cultures and imaging are essential in identifying infectious agents and assessing the extent of lesions.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
supporting_evidence: irregular, shallow ulcerated lesion on the tongue
tender lymph node in the left anterior cervical chain
additional_information_needed: biopsy results of the tongue lesion

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Oral Syphilis
supporting_evidence: tender lymph node in the neck
refuting_evidence: no mention of systemic symptoms like rash or fever

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Oral Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) Infection
refuting_evidence: culture of the tongue lesion was negative for HSV
additional_information_needed: history of previous oral herpes outbreaks

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Behçet's Disease
supporting_evidence: scattered areas of erythema and blisters on the lower legs
additional_information_needed: detailed history of recurrent oral/genital ulcers

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Traumatic Ulcer
key_features: painful ulcer at site of trauma
additional_information_needed: history of recent trauma to the tongue
observation of any sharp teeth or dental appliances

required.response: Acyclovir for 5 days, sulfamethoxazole–trimethoprim for 10 days, chlorhexidine gluconate rinses, narcotic analgesia, and clindamycin for 5 days.

teaching_points.content: Empirical treatment is often initiated based on clinical suspicion while awaiting diagnostic confirmation.
